exposure: Multiple infections (dengue and malaria) in pregnancy
cohort: The study included 85 pregnant women admitted with either dengue or malaria infections to a tertiary care hospital from 2011-2015.
finding: Pregnant women with dengue alone presented at an earlier gestational age (24 weeks), those with multiple infections delivered earlier (30 weeks), and women with malaria had a higher likelihood of low birth weight deliveries (mean 2394 g), with a 7% incidence of in-hospital deaths.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight 2394 g (for women with malaria)
gest_age: 24 weeks (gestational age at presentation for dengue), 30 weeks (gestational age at delivery for multiple infections)
